headline: Heavy rain forecast: BMD warns of heavy rainfall in 4 divisions
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department has advised inland river ports to hoist cautionary signal No. 1 as heavy rain is predicted for several regions.
details: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has forecast heavy rainfall in parts of the Rangpur, Mymensingh, Chattogram, and Sylhet divisions.
To manage the risk, the BMD has advised inland river ports to hoist cautionary signal No. 1.

A 24-hour forecast indicates light to moderate rain or thundershowers, accompanied by gusty winds and lightning, across many areas of Rangpur, Mymensingh, Khulna, Barisal, Chattogram, and Sylhet divisions.
The forecast also extends to some areas of Rajshahi and Dhaka divisions, with moderate to heavy rainfall predicted in some locations.
Temporary gusty or squally winds with speeds of 45-60kmph are expected to blow from the west or southwest over several regions, including Pabna, Mymensingh, and Sylhet, until Tuesday morning.
In the past 24 hours, Kutubdia Upazila of Cox's Bazar registered the highest nationwide rainfall at 150mm.

headline_marked: Armed forces [[granted magistracy powers in 6 areas]] until June 30
headline: Armed forces granted magistracy powers in 6 areas until June 30
summary: Commissioned officers of the army, navy, and air force can now arrest offenders and disperse unlawful assemblies to maintain public order.
details: The government has granted special executive magistracy powers to commissioned officers of the army, navy, and air force for nine days, effective until June 30.
The Ministry of Public Administration issued the notification on Monday evening, stating the order was made in the public interest.
These powers apply to three metropolitan areas—Dhaka, Chattogram, and Gazipur—and three districts: Narayanganj, Gopalganj, and Faridpur.
The move comes as troops are set to be deployed during the founding anniversary of the Bangladesh Awami League, whose activities currently remain banned.
Commissioned officers holding the rank of captain and above are vested with these powers, including those serving on deputation in the Coast Guard and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB).
Under the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, designated officers can now arrest offenders, conduct searches, and disperse unlawful assemblies.
These measures are intended to take preventive action and ensure public order is maintained across the specified regions.
caption:
Armed forces officers now have the power to arrest and disperse crowds in 6 key areas.

The government has granted special executive magistracy powers to commissioned officers of the army, navy, and air force for nine days, effective until June 30.

The Ministry of Public Administration issued the notification on Monday evening, stating the order was made in the public interest.

These powers apply to three metropolitan areas—Dhaka, Chattogram, and Gazipur—and three districts: Narayanganj, Gopalganj, and Faridpur.

The move comes as troops are set to be deployed during the founding anniversary of the Bangladesh Awami League, whose activities currently remain banned.

Commissioned officers holding the rank of captain and above are vested with these powers, including those serving on deputation in the Coast Guard and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB).

Under the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, designated officers can now arrest offenders, conduct searches, and disperse unlawful assemblies.

These measures are intended to take preventive action and ensure public order is maintained across the specified regions.
